summary: Searched TruthCore and the corpus for the exact theorem: none existed. Proved ¬∀ P Q : Prop, P ↔ Q from the two existing witnesses; ∃ P Q, P ∧ ¬ Q got no statement, since the conjunction of those witnesses suffices. Rejected reading: treating that theorem as refuting relativism or nihilism. It constrains a truth predicate only through the hypothesis Expressive, and the controls have models of no absolute truth with expressive relative truth, of total nihilism, of global profile variation and of gluts. A first draft of the capture clause expected a contradiction; ThesisSchemaModel shows disquotation with capture is satisfiable and yields only ¬ GlobalNoAbsoluteTruth, with no witness of absolute truth. Exhaustive negation had to be stated disjunctively: from ¬ truth p → truth (neg p), collapse gives only ¬¬ truth p constructively. Profile for elimination: under Expressive, or exclusion with exhaustion on inhabited contents, predicate collapse is excluded; without those bridges nothing beyond Prop collapse is. Eliminated corpus rivals: none; STMT-GLOBAL-NO-ABSOLUTE-TRUTH stays surviving and no refutes relation is added. Strongest remaining rival: relative-truth relativism with expressive relative predicates. Remaining gaps: no source reading of any relativist or nihilist; whether any rival accepts Expressive, capture or exhaustion is open.
